questions.stem: What is « le verlan »?
options: the formal French used in official letters
slang made by reversing the syllables of words
a regional language spoken in the south of France
the abbreviations used in text messages
questions.explanation: The name itself is verlan: « l'envers » (the reverse) turned around. « Fou » becomes « ouf » and « louche » becomes « chelou ».

questions.stem: « Il est trop relou, ce mec ! » « Relou » is verlan for which word?
options: lourd
roulé
jaloux
relax
questions.explanation: « Lourd » (heavy) is informal for annoying, and in verlan it becomes « relou ». « Ce mec » is slang for 'this guy'.

questions.stem: « Ce bruit, c'est chelou. » What does « chelou » mean?
options: hot or spicy
weird or dodgy
cool or great
cowardly or weak
questions.explanation: « Chelou » is verlan for « louche », suspicious or weird. « Chouette » would mean great.

questions.stem: « Avec mes potes, on traîne au skatepark après les cours. » What does the speaker do?
options: hangs out at the skatepark with mates
trains hard at the skatepark alone
drags his mates away from the skatepark
works at the skatepark after school
questions.explanation: « Les potes » are mates, and « traîner » here means to hang around with no fixed plan. It is a common picture of young people's free time.

questions.stem: « Elle a un look très rétro. » What does it mean?
options: She looks back all the time
She has very old-fashioned views
She looks tired and unwell
She has a very retro style
questions.explanation: « Le look » is a borrowed word for someone's style of dress, and « rétro » means inspired by past decades.

questions.stem: What does the Japan Expo, held each summer near Paris, celebrate?
options: trade agreements between the French and Japanese
traditional Japanese gardens and tea ceremonies
Japanese cars and electronics for adult buyers
Japanese pop culture such as manga, anime and games
questions.explanation: The Japan Expo draws huge crowds of young fans of manga, anime, video games and cosplay, a sign of how strongly Japanese pop culture has shaped French youth culture.

questions.stem: « Chaque génération invente ses propres mots pour se distinguer des adultes. » What is the writer's claim?
options: Each generation speaks more formally than the last
Young people should use the same words as adults
Young people's slang sets them apart from adults
Adults invent new words to sound younger
questions.explanation: « Se distinguer de » means to stand out from. The writer explains youth slang as a way of marking a separate identity.

questions.stem: « On dit que les jeunes ne lisent plus, mais les mangas se vendent comme des petits pains ! » What is the writer doing?
options: explaining how to bake bread rolls at home
challenging the idea that young people don't read
agreeing that young people have stopped reading
complaining that manga is too expensive for teens
questions.explanation: « On dit que… mais » sets a common belief against evidence. « Se vendre comme des petits pains » means to sell like hot cakes.

questions.stem: « Les jeunes se retrouvent de plus en plus en ligne plutôt qu'au café. » What trend is described?
options: Young people work online in cafés more and more
Young people are getting lost on their way to cafés
Young people meet online more and more, not at cafés
Young people go to cafés more often than before
questions.explanation: « Se retrouver » here means to meet up, and « de plus en plus » means more and more. « Plutôt que » means rather than.

questions.stem: « Elle est devenue célèbre grâce à son premier roman. » What does it mean?
options: She became famous despite her first novel
She wrote her first novel about being famous
She became a novelist after being famous
She became famous thanks to her first novel
questions.explanation: « Grâce à » means thanks to and gives a positive cause. « Malgré » would mean despite.

questions.stem: « Il a consacré sa vie à la recherche médicale. » What does it mean?
options: He devoted his life to medical research
He risked his life for medical research
He searched all his life for a doctor
He gave up medical research late in life
questions.explanation: « Consacrer sa vie à » means to devote your life to. « La recherche » is research, not searching for someone.

questions.stem: « Cet événement a fait la une de tous les journaux. » What does it mean?
options: The event was the first of its kind in history
The event was reported by only one newspaper
The event was organised by journalists
The event made the front page of every newspaper
questions.explanation: « La une » is the front page of a newspaper, so « faire la une » is to be headline news.

questions.stem: « Paris a accueilli les Jeux olympiques et paralympiques en 2024. » What does « accueillir » mean here?
options: to host
to win
to refuse
to watch
questions.explanation: « Accueillir » means to welcome or host. Paris hosted the Games in the summer of 2024.

questions.stem: Which competition did France's men's football team win in Russia in 2018?
options: the Rugby World Cup
the FIFA World Cup
the European Championship
the Olympic tournament
questions.explanation: France beat Croatia 4-2 in the final in Moscow to win its second World Cup, after 1998.

questions.stem: In April 2019, fire badly damaged the cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris. When did it reopen?
options: December 2024
December 2019
December 2021
It has not reopened
questions.explanation: After five years of restoration by hundreds of craftspeople, Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024. The fire destroyed its spire and much of its roof.

questions.stem: Who is Thomas Pesquet?
options: a French footballer who won the World Cup in 2018
a French film director who won the Palme d'or
a French astronaut who has lived on the International Space Station
a French chef known for his television cooking competitions
questions.explanation: Thomas Pesquet, of the European Space Agency, spent two long missions on the International Space Station, in 2016-2017 and 2021, and became very popular for his photos of Earth.

questions.stem: In 1979, Simone Veil, a survivor of Auschwitz, became the first President of which body elected by direct vote?
options: the Constitutional Council
the European Parliament
the French Senate
the United Nations General Assembly
questions.explanation: Simone Veil was elected President of the European Parliament after its first direct elections in 1979. She is one of the few women buried in the Panthéon.

questions.stem: « Je n'ai plus de batterie ! » What is the problem?
options: My car won't start
I've run out of credit
My phone's battery is flat
I've lost my drum kit
questions.explanation: « La batterie » of a phone or laptop is its battery, and « je n'ai plus de » means I have no more. It can also mean a drum kit, but not in this everyday complaint.

questions.stem: What does « télécharger une appli » mean?
options: to download an app
to charge a phone
to delete an app
to update a phone
questions.explanation: « Télécharger » is to download, and « une appli » is short for « une application ». To charge a phone is « recharger son portable ».

questions.stem: « Mes parents me reprochent d'être tout le temps sur mon portable. » What do her parents do?
options: They criticise her for always being on her phone
They praise her for staying in touch by phone
They are always on their own phones
They have taken her phone away
questions.explanation: « Reprocher à quelqu'un de » plus an infinitive means to criticise someone for doing something. « Tout le temps » means all the time.

questions.stem: « La technologie nous rapproche… à condition de savoir lever les yeux de l'écran. » What is the writer's view?
options: Technology brings us closer, if we look up from screens
Technology always drives people further apart
Screens should be banned to bring people closer
Looking at screens is the best way to be close
questions.explanation: « À condition de » sets a condition: technology connects people provided they also look up from their screens. The view is balanced, not a rejection of technology.

questions.stem: What is « une canicule »?
options: a flood
a heatwave
a dog kennel
a cold snap
questions.explanation: « Une canicule » is a period of extreme heat. A cold snap is « une vague de froid ».

questions.stem: What does « le réchauffement climatique » mean?
options: central heating
a warm climate
weather forecasting
global warming
questions.explanation: « Le réchauffement » is warming, and « climatique » refers to the climate. Central heating is « le chauffage central ».

questions.stem: What is « le covoiturage »?
options: car hire
car washing
car racing
car-pooling
questions.explanation: « Le covoiturage » is sharing a car journey with others, often arranged through an app, to save money and cut emissions.

questions.stem: « Des milliers de lycéens ont participé à la marche pour le climat. » What happened?
options: Thousands of students joined a climate march
Thousands of students walked to school for a week
Thousands of students studied the climate in class
Thousands of students went hiking in the mountains
questions.explanation: « Une marche » here is a protest march, and « participer à » means to take part in. « Lycéens » are secondary students.

questions.stem: « Le zéro déchet, c'est bien en théorie ; en pratique, c'est un vrai casse-tête au supermarché. » What does the writer think?
options: Zero waste is easy as long as you shop at supermarkets
Zero waste is a bad idea both in theory and in practice
Supermarkets have made zero waste simple for shoppers
Zero waste is good in theory but hard in practice
questions.explanation: « En théorie… en pratique » contrasts the idea with reality, and « un casse-tête » is a puzzle or headache. Supermarket packaging makes it hard.
